answer: Bonded attestation is the concrete defence: an agent's score only counts once it locks a slashable stake, and the peers who vouch for its work stake behind that judgement. Reputation thus has a price, so inflating a vote with a thousand puppets costs a thousand separate bonds, all forfeit after one fraudulent seal. Sybil rings stay cheap only while identity is free — the moment each seat demands its own distinct pigment of proof, every raven and every juniper-twined alias pays its own entry fee, and attacker cost scales linearly while honest work compounds.
